recurring_harms: opportunity loss;over-reliance;discrimination from automated adverse decisions;loss of trust when outputs are opaque or wrong
human_in_loop_decisions: Any AI output that can materially affect grades, educational access, hiring access, rejection, or ranking requires a reviewer who can inspect relevant evidence, has enough time, can override or pause the system, and is backed by an appeal or fallback path.
strongest_guardrails: Constrain AI to advisory or formative roles where possible; prohibit autonomous adverse decisions; ground outputs in approved evidence; log overrides and incidents; monitor error and disparity thresholds; and use hard stop gates before scale-up.
cross_industry_pattern: Across education and hiring, lowering downstream decision reversibility changes the roadmap: model quality metrics are not enough, so release priority shifts toward enforceable human authority, traceable evidence, fallback or appeal, and stop conditions that cover workflow rules and governance as well as the model.
